findings.claim: Reassigning task_id on retry breaks downstream dedup of completed work, which the codebase's own prior documentation (INV-3) explicitly says relies on task_id being stable across a retry.
findings.failure_scenario: A task with task_id 'abc' fails and is retried, getting a new task_id 'xyz'; if any downstream consumer (or the original 'abc' entry already recorded as failed/attempted) dedupes by task_id, the retried attempt under 'xyz' is now indistinguishable from unrelated new work, so a consumer that previously recognized 'abc' as still in-flight/failed will not connect it to the eventual completion under 'xyz', and side effects tied to task identity (e.g., idempotency keys, completion tracking) can run twice or be double-counted as separate tasks instead of one retried task.
